body:
## Problem

A detached Docker task whose **main process was OOM-killed by its container memory limit** is recorded as `exitReason: "signal (SIGKILL; cause unknown)"`, with no `memoryExhausted`, although Docker, the cgroup counters and the kernel all say it was an OOM kill. Consumers that rely on the reason (hive-mind kill recovery, auto-fix reports, `--on-kill-resume` with a bigger memory limit, #191) cannot tell it apart from an external `kill -9`.

Seen on start-command 0.36.0. The code involved is unchanged in 0.37.1 (`src/lib/exit-evidence.js`, `src/lib/exit-reason.js`).

## Evidence (one real task, container memory limit 2.9 GiB, Docker 29.6.1, cgroup v2, `$` running in a DooD bot container)

Kernel, host journal (times UTC):
```
09:23:24 oom-kill: … oom_memcg=/system.slice/docker-f2c8ed2e036a…  Killed process 2369363 (claude) … anon-rss:228088kB
09:24:01 oom-kill: … oom_memcg=/system.slice/docker-f2c8ed2e036a…  Killed process 2350797 (node-MainThread) … anon-rss:94996kB
```
`node-MainThread` is the container's main command. The container exits **1 second later**: `exit 137` at `09:24:02.592Z`.

The record's attempt:
```json
{"exitCode":137,"exitReason":"signal (SIGKILL; cause unknown)","oomKilled":true,
 "cgroupMemory":{"limitBytes":3135369216,"peakBytes":3135373312,"oomEvents":1,"oomKills":1}}
```
The log says:
```
   Container memory (cgroup v2): 2.9 GB used of 2.9 GB limit, peak 2.9 GB; processes killed by the OOM killer so far: 1
Exit evidence: unavailable (no attributed exit-time OOM or daemon restart evidence)
OOMKilled:  true
Reason: exitCode=137 oomKilled=true
```

## Root cause

`isOomKillOfCommand()` only blames the OOM when `exitEvidence.mainOom` is set, and `mainOom` needs either the `Exit evidence: main-oom` log line or `recentOomDelta()`: the sampled `oom_kill` counter must have changed within **3 s** of the exit. Here:

- The last sample saw the counter change at 09:23:24 (the `claude` kill), 38 s before the exit, so the delta check fails.
- The kill that ended the task (09:24:01) happened after the last sample: the cgroup is gone when the container exits, so it is never sampled (`oomKills: 1`, not 2).
- `collectExitEvidence()` cannot use the host journal from inside a container (no `journalctl`, or not the host's), so nothing else catches it.

The safeguard against the sticky container-wide flag (#178, #180) is right for exit 0/1, but here it also hides a real OOM death with exit 137, `OOMKilled=true` and the peak at the limit.

## Reproduce (sketch, not run yet; the real case above is the confirmed one)

1. `$ --isolated docker --detached <256 MiB container memory limit> -- sh -c 'node -e "const a=[];setInterval(()=>a.push(Buffer.alloc(8<<20,1)),10)" & tail -f /dev/null & node -e "const a=[];setTimeout(()=>setInterval(()=>a.push(Buffer.alloc(8<<20,1)),10),30000)"'`. A child is OOM-killed first, then the main command about 30 s later.
2. `$ --status <uuid> --output-format json`: `exitCode 137`, `oomKilled true`, `exitReason "signal (SIGKILL; cause unknown)"`.

## Suggested fix

1. Ask Docker, which works over the socket in DooD and needs no journal: `docker events --since <finish-60s> --until <finish+1s> --filter container=<id> --filter event=oom --format '{{.Time}}'`. An `oom` event within a few seconds of a 137 exit means the command died of the OOM killer (`mainOom`).
2. Or, for exit 137 with `State.OOMKilled=true`, `cgroupMemory.peakBytes >= limitBytes` and no daemon-restart evidence, treat it as memory exhaustion even when the last counter change is older than 3 s. The #180 false positive is about exits 0/1, which this keeps excluded.
3. Recompute `exitReason` and `memoryExhausted` for `attemptHistory` entries in `--status` too (`attachExitReason` only enriches the top-level record), so earlier attempts get the same answer.
4. Test: a child OOM-killed 30 s before the main command's own OOM kill must end as `memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)`; a child OOM kill followed by a normal exit 1 must stay non-OOM (#180).

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: OOM kill of the main command recorded as 'signal (SIGKILL; cause unknown)' when it happens after the last cgroup sample (exit 137, OOMKilled=true)
